data.narrative:
Oxide Computer Company, a Series C semiconductor design firm founded by Steve Tuck and Bryan Cantrill, is valued within a competitive peer set of 11 total comparables—3 public (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. The company has raised $389M to date.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $389M total raised proxy, yielding $661M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks Oxide against three same-sector, same-stage private companies: Etched ($5.0B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and DEEPX ($529M). The median of this peer set is $2.0B, establishing an upper anchor despite wide dispersion ($529M to $5.0B).

Triangulation of both methods produces a valuation range of $562M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.3B. The low end reflects stage-progression conservatism; the high end reflects peer-median positioning. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.7x stage multiplier for frontier semiconductor ventures—where capital intensity and TAM ambition vary significantly—and the relevance of the peer set's wide dispersion, suggesting heterogeneous risk profiles or market timing effects within Series C semiconductor financing.
